findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the surface to the right of the dish machine is not sealed to the wall. The inspector educated that surfaces that cannot be easily moved must be sealed to the wall to ensure that debris does not accumulate underneath. The surface can be sealed using caulking, flex tape, or another method. Ensure that the surface to the right of the dish machine is sealed to be a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Observed the facility was storing previously wet wiping cloths in the triple sink and dry sanitizer buckets overnight. The PIC stated the cloths had been used yesterday for cleaning dishes. The inspector educated that dry clean wiping cloths may be stored anywhere but wet in-use wiping cloths must be stored in chemical sanitizer solutions between uses. When they are done being used the wiping cloths must be laundered. They CANNOT be left overnight and used the next day without laundering. The wiping clothes were removed from service to be laundered during the inspection. Ensure that wiping cloths are always stored correctly and laundered daily.

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed the surface to the right of the dish machine is not sealed to the wall. The inspector educated that surfaces that cannot be easily moved must be sealed to the wall to ensure that debris does not accumulate underneath. This can be accomplished by caulking the surface to the wall (this is done correctly on the surface to the left of the dish machine). The surface must be sealed to the wall by the next routine inspection. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Inspector observed that the dish machine had a chlorine concentration of at or near 0 ppm based on inspector test strips. The container which held the sanitizer solution was empty. Operator immediately replaced the container of sanitizer and primed the machine to ensure proper sanitizer concentrations are in use. Upon testing, inspector observed a concentration of approximately 50 ppm chlorine in the dish machine. Violation has been corrected on site and no follow-up is required at this time. Ensure that sanitizer concentrations are above minimum required values at all times. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple cans in the walk-in cooler with dents along upper/lower seams. These dents were significant in depth to bring the integrity of the can seals into question. Cans which are dented along seams raise a concern for food borne botulism. As such, cans must be inspected upon arrival for dents and discarded/refused when noted on arrival. Cans which are identified as dented during operations must immediately be removed from storage with cans used for serving food to prevent accidental usage. Ensure that cans are checked for integrity upon delivery to the facility. Foods are sourced from SYSCO and the school district. All dented cans have been removed from storage and separated from intact product. Corrected on site. No follow-up required at this time. 

3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The hood above the stove and ovens is observed to be soiled with dust and other debris. Several pieces of equipment are unused during operations and no grease is used in the cooking process (i.e. frying). The hood is not routinely cleaned/services because it is not utilized in this facility. The hood must remain clean and dust must be removed to prevent potential contamination of foods being cooked underneath it.

Fans in the facility have blades/guards which are soiled with dust. These fans present a hazard in that they blow air potentially contaminated with this dust and debris across areas where food and/or cleaning activities are occurring. Ensure that the fans are cleaned often enough to prevent the accumulation of dust, residue and debris. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Areas underneath and behind large pieces of equipment are observed to be soiled with food debris, cob webs and dead pests. These hard to reach areas must be included in a routine cleaning schedule at a frequency that precludes the accumulation of debris that has the potential to contaminate food and other items used in the food preparation and cleaning processes and to prevent insects/pests from becoming a problem at the facility. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 (B) Food prep was underway for lunch service, and sani-bucket was not available for use. Sani-bucket was prepared during inspection. Ensure the sani-bucket is prepared and available prior to beginning food handling, which includes placing prepared, heat and serve foods on a tray.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:

Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. Faucet was shut off without a barrier, and handle of paper towel dispenser was touched to retrieve paper towels after handwashing was completed. Proper technique was discussed, and hands were re-washed using proper technique prior to continuing with food prep.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.
Educational handout were provided for proper handwashing technique.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-304.15(A): Employee was observed adjusting face mask and glasses with gloved hands and returned to service line to count and handle clean trays for lunch service. Proper glove use was discussed. Soiled gloves were discarded. 
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.
NOTE: Be mindful of personal habits and ensure glove changes occur after touching anything unrelated to food handling and/or working with clean equipment, dishes, and utensils. 
Educational handout was provided for proper glove use.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-203.11: Food thermometer used for checking final cook temperatures was reading at ~90F at room temperature. Ice water solution was used to check all thermometers scaled 0-220F. The thermometer reading at ~90F was at 50F in ice water, while the other food thermometer was reading at 32F. Manager needed to get a tool to complete calibration of the thermometer reading at 50F. In the meantime, staff will begin using the thermometer that was reading at 32F. Cleaning and maintenance of food thermometers were discussed.
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-904.11 Forks were observed in the utensil caddy stored with the food contact surface presented out. Employee was observed handling forks on and around the food contact surface and was not wearing gloves. Employee was advised on handwashing and glove use when handling utensils stored in this manner. Employee stated hands were washed prior to handling the forks. Gloves need to also be worn when, based on storage practice, it is not possible to avoid touching the food contact surface of utensils. Another option would be to store the utensils with the handles presented out of the caddy to avoid touching the food contact surface when retrieving utensils.
Cleaned and sanitized utensils shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent contamination of food- and lip-contact surfaces. Utensils not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by employees.
